earliest_witness: Yinqueshan bamboo slips, Linyi (tombs dated to roughly 140–118 BCE; found 1972)
structure: Thirteen short chapters, in Giles's titles: Laying Plans; Waging War; Attack by Stratagem; Tactical Dispositions; Energy; Weak Points and Strong; Manoeuvring; Variation in Tactics; The Army on the March; Terrain; The Nine Situations; The Attack by Fire; The Use of Spies.
summary: Ancient Chinese military text in 13 chapters, attributed to Sun Wu (Sun Tzu). Confirmed by bamboo-slip copies buried in the 2nd century BCE; probably compiled in the 5th–4th century BCE, perhaps over time.
versions_and_translations: Yinqueshan bamboo-slip copy, before c. 118 BCE (SRC-000027)
Han shu bibliography lists a Sunzi in 82 chapters with diagrams (CLM-000065)
Cao Cao (155–220 CE): earliest surviving commentary
French Jesuit missionary's translation, late 18th century
Roger Ames, 1993: first English translation to use the Yinqueshan slips (not yet consulted)
